pll1d22c1-d1e3503.summary: Announces the treatise on the diversity of names used for the ineffable Unity and Trinity, and the ways something is said of it.

pll1d22c1-d1e3506.summary: With De Trinitate VIII, holds that some names belong distinctly to single persons and are said only of them, some signify the unity of essence and are said of each singly and all together, and some are said of God metaphorically and by likeness.
claims: Some names are proper to single persons.
Some names signify the unity of essence.
Some names are said of God metaphorically.

pll1d22c1-d1e3528.summary: Cites Ambrose's threefold distinction: names showing the property of deity (generation, Son, Word), names expressing the truth of divine majesty and eternal unity (wisdom, power, truth), and names said by transference and likeness (splendor, character, mirror).
claims: Names of property include generation, Son, Word.
Names of unity include wisdom, power, truth.
Names of likeness include splendor, character, mirror.

pl-l1d22c1.summary: Begins the treatise on divine names: the diversity of names used for the ineffable Unity and Trinity and the modes of predication. With Augustine, some names belong distinctly to single persons, some signify the unity of essence and are said of each and all, and some are said of God metaphorically. Ambrose gives a parallel threefold distinction: names of property (generation, Son, Word), of eternal unity (wisdom, power, truth), and of likeness (splendor, character, mirror).
claims: Some divine names belong to single persons.
Some signify the unity of essence and are said of each person and all together.
Some are said of God by transference and likeness.
Names of property include Son and Word; of unity, wisdom and power; of likeness, splendor and mirror.
